newsitem.title: CHILE: Massad takes office as Chile Central Bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Massad takes office as Chile Central Bank chief.

text.p: Economist Carlos Massad took office as president and board member of the Central Bank, after his appointment was confirmed in an official decree over the weekend.

Massad's swearing-in ended a long political wrangle that began when rightists in Congress refused to confirm his appointment because they said he was too close to President Eduardo Frei's Christian Democratic Party to guarantee the bank's autonomy.

The Senate rejected his appointment, but then approved it in a second vote. Moving quickly to end any further political bickering over the appointment, the government published the decree making Massad's appointment official on Saturday.
He replaced Roberto Zahler, who quit in June after accusing the board of granting too many concessions to private banks in their negotiations to reschedule payments on their debt to the Central Bank.
Massad, Frei's former health minister and a Central Bank president in the late 1960s, said last week he would complete Zahler's term to late 1997 and possibly stay in the post beyond then.
